name: Signal-triggered, event-driven
when_to_use: Signal coverage is dense enough that most contacts carry a recent, dated trigger. Selecting it without that coverage produces a sequence that never fires: the first touch waits on an event that never arrives.
rationale: Timing comes from the prospect's behaviour rather than a calendar. The touch fires because something happened - a role change, a fraud-role posting, a public incident - so the opening line is a fact about them from this week rather than a guess. Signal-triggered sequences report 8-15% reply rates against 2-5% for static lists, which is a larger effect than any copy change in this pipeline.
cites: research/01-discipline-and-pipeline.md (frontier 2026 pattern: adaptive, event-driven not calendar-driven)
evidence_note: The reply-rate spread is vendor-benchmark, uncontrolled, and confounded: signal-triggered lists are also better-qualified lists. The mechanism to trust is recency, not the multiplier.

trigger.fires_on: any scored signal fresher than its decay window
trigger.why: A trigger older than its decay window is worse than no trigger. Opening with a month-old event tells the reader this was queued, not noticed.

touches.intent: Open on the signal itself. The reason for writing today is the first thing the reader sees.
constraints: the signal must be dated and verifiable
never imply surveillance - cite the public source
cites: research/04 §5.3 (no surface personalization as a substitute for relevance)

touches.intent: Connect the signal to the consequence the reader has not priced yet.
Close the loop while the trigger is still recent enough to reference.
constraints: drop the touch entirely if the trigger has aged past max_age_days

branches.why: The premise of the sequence has expired. Continuing means opening on a stale fact.
